transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I guess I came in because… nothing really feels like mine anymore, if that makes sense. Like, the things I used to care about, the things that made me feel like I was me—I just don’t feel anything for them now.

I used to get excited about murals, you know, seeing them around town or thinking about colors and lines and what someone was trying to say with them. I used to run, and even if I wasn’t fast or anything, there was a feeling to it. Basketball too—watching it, playing a little, talking about it. And even at work, making a really good drink, getting it just right, that used to give me some pride.

Now I just kind of stand there. I look at the same stuff and it’s like… nothing. Like I’m watching someone else’s life from across the room. I don’t care about any of it the way I used to, and that’s what scared me enough to come in.
Can you tell me if you’ve lost interest in those activities completely, or if you still want to do them but just can’t seem to feel anything from them?

I think it’s more like… I don’t even really want to do them anymore, not in the way I used to. Or maybe I go through the motion of wanting to, because I remember that I used to be that person. Like with murals, I’ll see one and I know, in my head, that normally I’d stop and look at the details, the colors, the way the lines are done, all of that. I used to get this little spark from it. Now I just look at it and it’s flat. Like it has nothing to do with me.

Same with running or basketball. It’s not even that I’m sitting there wishing I could enjoy it and then failing. It’s more like the wanting part got shut off too. And at work, making a good drink… I know when I’ve done it right, I know what it’s supposed to feel like to take pride in that, but I just kind of stand there and do it. It doesn’t land anywhere.

So I guess the honest answer is both, but mostly I’ve lost interest. I don’t care about any of it the way I used to, and that’s what scared me.
Have you noticed that your mood has been down or depressed most of the time, even outside of not feeling interested in those activities?

I’m not totally sure how to separate those things, honestly. Like… I don’t walk around thinking, “I’m sad,” exactly. It’s not always that clear. A lot of the time it’s more like everything is heavy or muted, like the color got turned down on the whole day.

But if you mean, do I feel low even when I’m not specifically thinking about murals or running or work or whatever… yeah, I think so. I mean, I don’t know if I’d call it depressed every minute, because sometimes I’m just kind of blank, or I’m distracted by whatever I’m doing. But underneath it, there’s this dragged-down feeling that seems to be there most of the time.

It’s hard to explain because I keep second-guessing myself. Like maybe I’m just tired, or maybe I’m just in a bad stretch. But it doesn’t really lift the way a normal bad mood would. It’s just there, kind of sitting on everything.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep or appetite lately, or do you find yourself feeling worse about yourself than usual?

Yeah… sleep, definitely. I mean, appetite I’m not really sure how to answer right now, but sleep has been bad.

I’ll be exhausted by the time I lie down, like my body feels completely done, especially after work. But as soon as I’m in bed, my head just starts going. It’s like it picks up every little thing I did wrong that day and plays it back at me. If I messed up an order, or took too long with someone’s drink, or said something awkward to a customer, or even just looked like I didn’t know what I was doing… it all comes back. And it doesn’t feel like normal thinking, exactly. It feels like I’m stuck reviewing evidence against myself.

So I’m lying there tired, but I can’t drop off because my mind won’t shut up. Then when I finally do sleep, it’s not like I sleep through. I’ve been waking up around four or five in the morning, and once I’m awake, that’s usually it. I just lie there and try to force myself back down, but it doesn’t happen. Then I’m just waiting for the day to start, already feeling worn out before anything’s even happened.
Can you tell me if your appetite has changed lately—like if you're eating more or less than usual—or if you've noticed any recent weight loss or gain without trying?

Yeah… I think I’ve been eating less. Not in some planned way, not like I’m trying to lose weight or anything. It’s more like food just doesn’t occur to me the way it used to.

Most days I’ll get through a big part of the shift and realize I haven’t eaten because my hands start shaking behind the bar. Like I’ll be reaching for something or trying to pour and I notice that trembly feeling, and then it hits me that I’ve had maybe coffee or nothing, and it’s already way too late in the day. But even then it’s not like I suddenly feel hungry in a normal way. It’s more like, “Oh, I guess I should put something in my body so I don’t fall over.”

Sometimes after closing I’ll grab whatever’s around, like a few bites of something cold, something that’s been sitting there, and I’ll just kind of force it down. And then I feel sick looking at it, or sick thinking about eating more. It’s strange because I know I need to eat, but the idea of food feels… I don’t know, pointless or kind of gross.

As far as weight, I don’t know exactly. I haven’t really been checking. My clothes maybe feel a little different, but I couldn’t tell you a number. It’s more the eating itself that’s changed. I just forget, and then when I remember, I don’t want it.
Have you noticed yourself moving more slowly than usual, or on the contrary, feeling restless or unable to sit still, especially during the day?

I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed it in a clear way, like I don’t think I’m pacing around the room all day or anything like that. And I don’t know that I’d say I’m moving dramatically slower either.

I mean, at work there are moments where I feel like I’m dragging, like everything takes more effort than it should, but I don’t know if that’s the same thing you’re asking. It’s not like someone has said, “Why are you moving so slow?” or “Sit still,” at least not that I can think of. Sometimes I’m just standing there and it takes me a second to get going, but that might just be me being tired or distracted.

So… I guess I’d say I haven’t really noticed either one in a definite way. If it’s happening, I’m not very aware of it.
Have you had any thoughts about not wanting to live, or that life isn't worth living?

I… I don’t really know how to answer that cleanly. I don’t think I have some clear thing to tell you, like a plan or anything I’ve decided. It’s more… sometimes everything feels so heavy that I catch myself thinking, “What is the point of doing this again tomorrow?” But then I don’t know if that’s the same as not wanting to live.

I guess I’ve had moments where life feels kind of not worth much, or like I’m just taking up space and making things harder, but it’s hard for me to sort out what’s a real thought and what’s just me being exhausted and worn down. I haven’t really sat there and made a decision about it. It’s more like these thoughts pass through, and I try not to look straight at them too long.

So… I’m not sure. I wouldn’t say I’m actively trying to do anything to myself, but yeah, I guess there are times it feels like it would be easier if I didn’t have to keep going.
Have you noticed that you have significantly less energy than usual, or that even small tasks feel exhausting to you?

Yeah. That part I have noticed, pretty strongly.

It’s not just being tired at the end of the night, because I’m used to being tired after a shift. I’ve been bartending long enough to know what normal tired feels like. This is different. It’s like I start out already behind somehow. By the time I carry a couple cases of liquor or set up the well, my body feels like I’ve already worked a double, even if I barely did anything earlier that day.

And those aren’t even huge tasks, you know? They’re things I’ve done a thousand times without thinking. Stocking bottles, cutting fruit, dragging a trash bag out, wiping everything down before we open. Lately it feels like every step has a weight tied to it. I’ll do one thing and then have to stand there for a second, not because it was impossible, but because I feel drained in this weird, deep way.

It’s embarrassing, honestly. I keep telling myself, “Come on, just do the next thing,” but even small stuff feels like I have to talk myself into it. Not because I don’t know how to do it, just because there’s no energy there. Like the tank is empty before the day even starts.
How long have you been feeling this way? Have these symptoms been going on for at least two weeks straight, or have they come and gone during that time?

It’s been… about two months now, I think. I’m trying to place it because I didn’t wake up one morning and go, “Okay, now I’m like this.” It kind of settled in after the bar got bought out.

That’s when everything I had been working toward there got changed around, and after that it’s like I just never really got back to feeling normal. So yes, it’s definitely been more than two weeks. It hasn’t been like one bad weekend and then I was fine. There are maybe hours or parts of a day where I’m distracted enough that I’m not thinking about it as much, but overall it’s been pretty steady for those two months. It’s just been hanging around.
Have you had periods like this before, where you felt this way for weeks at a time, or is this the first time you’ve experienced something like this?

I don’t know… I’m trying to think back and be fair about it.

I’ve had rough patches before, sure. I mean, I’m 51, I’ve had jobs go sideways, relationships be stressful, money be tight, all the normal life stuff. There have been times I was down or worn out for a while, but I don’t know if it was like this, exactly. I can’t really point to another time and say, “Yes, that was the same thing for weeks.”

Maybe there were stretches where I was in a bad mood or felt beat up by life, but this feels harder to shake. Or maybe I just didn’t pay attention before and kept working through it. I’m not sure. I don’t want to say something definite if I can’t really remember it clearly.

So… I guess I’d say I’ve had bad periods before, but I don’t know that I’ve had one quite like this, going on this long and feeling this heavy.
Have you ever had a period in your life before this one—lasting at least two weeks—where your mood was down most days and you lost interest in things you usually care about?

I’m not really sure, honestly.

I’ve had times where I was in a slump, or where life felt pretty flat for a while, but when you say “at least two weeks” and “down most days” and also losing interest in things I usually care about… I don’t know if I can confidently say yes to that from before.

There were periods where I was unhappy, sure. Like, I’ve gone through stretches where work was stressful or I didn’t feel like going out much, but I don’t know if that was the same thing or if it was just being worn down by whatever was happening at the time. I guess I never really tracked it that closely. I’d just keep working, go home, sleep, repeat, and not think of it as some clear episode.

So I don’t want to say no like it’s impossible, but I also can’t point to a specific time before this where I know I felt that way for two weeks or more and stopped caring about things. I just… I’m not sure.

Can you recall if you’ve ever had a time before this one—lasting at least two weeks—where you felt down most days and stopped caring about things you usually enjoy, even if it wasn’t exactly the same as what you’re feeling now?

I’m trying to pull one out, and I just… I can’t really land on one clearly.

I mean, if you asked me, “Have you ever been unhappy for a couple weeks?” I’d probably say yes, because life has had plenty of stretches like that. But when you put it together that way — down most days, for at least two weeks, and not caring about the things I usually enjoy — I don’t know. I don’t have a clean memory of that happening before.

There were times where I didn’t go out much, or I’d just work and come home and not do a whole lot, but I don’t know if that was because I’d stopped caring or because I was tired, or busy, or just in a routine. I’ve always been the kind of person who just keeps moving and doesn’t sit there measuring how bad it is, so looking back, it’s kind of blurry.

So… I can’t honestly say yes. It might’ve happened in some milder way, but I don’t remember a definite period like this before.
Can you recall if there was ever a time before this current period when you felt down most days and lost interest in things you usually care about for at least two weeks in a row?

I know you’ve asked it a couple ways, and I’m not trying to dodge it. I just genuinely don’t have a clean answer.

When I think back, I can remember being tired of things, or not wanting to deal with people, or just getting through work and going home and not doing much. But whether that was me being down most days and actually losing interest in things I cared about for two straight weeks… I don’t know. I didn’t really keep track like that, and at the time I don’t think I would’ve described it that way.

So if I’m being honest, I can’t recall a definite time before this where I’d say yes, that happened for at least two weeks in a row. Maybe there were stretches that looked similar from the outside, but in my memory it’s blurry. This current one stands out more to me than anything I can remember before.

Can you think back as far as you can—years ago if needed—and tell me if there was ever a time when you felt down most days and stopped caring about things you usually enjoy for two weeks or more, even if you didn’t seek help for it?

I’ve been trying to go back as far as I can while you’re asking, like even back years ago, and I still don’t come up with a clear “yes.”

I can remember rough patches, definitely. Times where I was worn out, or kind of withdrawn, or where I didn’t feel like doing much besides working and getting through the day. And there were probably weeks where, if you’d looked at me from the outside, you might’ve said I seemed down or not very interested in things. But in my own memory, it’s hard to separate that from just being tired, or stressed, or stuck in a routine.

The “two weeks or more” part is what I keep getting hung up on, because I just didn’t think about my life in those terms. I wasn’t marking days on a calendar or saying, “Okay, this has been going on every day.” I’d just sort of push through it.

So… no, I can’t honestly think of a definite time before this where I know I felt down most days and stopped caring about things I usually enjoy for two weeks or more. Maybe something close happened, but I don’t have a clear memory I can point to and say, yes, that was it.

Can you think back to any point in your life before this current two-month period when you had a clear time—whether or not you sought help—where you felt down most days and lost interest in things you usually care about for at least two weeks in a row?

I know I’m probably sounding like I’m circling the same answer, but no, I can’t really point to a clear time before these last couple months where I’d say that happened.

I’ve had periods in my life where I was unhappy, or where I got kind of flat and just did the bare minimum, but I can’t honestly say I remember it as, “I was down most days and stopped caring about things for two weeks straight.” Maybe if someone had been watching me closely back then, they might say something looked off, but from inside my own head, it’s not clear like that.

This time feels different in the sense that I can actually recognize it as a stretch, like it’s been going on. Before this, it’s more like scattered memories of being tired or withdrawn, not a definite episode I can mark out. So I don’t think I can give you a real yes to that.

Looking back over your entire life, can you recall any time—before these last two months—when you had a period that lasted at least two weeks where you felt down most days and stopped caring about things you usually enjoy?

I’ve been turning that over while you’ve been asking, and I still don’t have a solid one to give you.

I mean, over my whole life? Sure, I’ve had bad stretches. I’ve had times where I was worn down, where I wasn’t exactly excited about anything, where I just went to work and came home and didn’t make plans. But when you ask it that specific way — down most days, and not caring about things I usually enjoy, for at least two weeks — I can’t honestly say, “Yes, I remember that happening before.”

Part of the problem is I didn’t think about myself that way back then. I wasn’t sitting there counting days or paying attention to whether it was every day or most days. I’d just call it being tired, or being in a rut, or needing to keep moving. So there might’ve been times that were close, but I don’t have a clear memory of a definite two-week period before these last couple months.

So my answer is… I don’t recall one clearly. Not before this.

Looking back over your entire life, can you recall any time before these last two months when you had a period that lasted at least two weeks where you felt down most days and stopped caring about things you usually enjoy?

I know I’ve answered this a few times, and I’m not trying to be difficult, but I really don’t think I can give you a clear yes on that.

When I look back over my life, there are definitely times I’d call bad stretches. Like periods where I was just kind of dragging myself through the day, not making much effort socially, not really excited about anything. But I can’t separate out in my memory whether that was actually feeling down most days and not caring about things for two weeks straight, or whether it was more just being tired, stressed, or stuck in the same routine.

I didn’t really keep track of things that way back then. I’d just keep working, come home, maybe keep to myself, and figure that was just life for a while. So there might have been times that looked close from the outside, but I don’t have a specific period before these last two months where I can honestly say, “Yes, that was definitely at least two weeks of feeling down most days and losing interest.”

So… no, not that I can clearly recall.
Before these last two months, can you clearly remember having a time when you felt down most days and lost interest in things you usually care about for at least two weeks in a row?

No… not clearly. I know that probably sounds like I’m repeating myself, but I don’t want to say yes just to give an answer if I can’t actually remember it that way.

Before these last two months, I can remember being worn out, or bored with things, or keeping to myself for a while. There were times where life felt kind of gray, I guess. But I can’t point to a stretch and say, yes, for two weeks in a row I was down most days and had stopped caring about the things I normally care about.

It’s more like scattered memories than a clear block of time. So I’d have to say no, not one that I can clearly remember.
Before these last two months, can you clearly remember having a time when you felt down most days and lost interest in things you usually care about for at least two weeks in a row?

No, before this I can’t really say that I clearly remember a stretch like that.

What I can say clearly is that this time has been going on about two months now. It started around when the bar was bought out, because that changed everything I’d been working toward. Before that, I might’ve had rough patches or been tired from work, but this particular kind of feeling — where things just dropped off and I stopped feeling like myself — that’s been these last two months.

doctor.intent: Establish the patient's reason for seeking help
doctor.question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

target_item.name: Loss_of_Interest
target_item.manifestation: I came in because nothing feels like mine anymore—I used to get excited about murals, runs, basketball, even making a good drink, and now I just stand there like I don't care about any of it.
target_item.reason: This is the first reply of the consultation, so I should return the chief complaint symptom code.

patient.answer:
I guess I came in because… nothing really feels like mine anymore, if that makes sense. Like, the things I used to care about, the things that made me feel like I was me—I just don’t feel anything for them now.

I used to get excited about murals, you know, seeing them around town or thinking about colors and lines and what someone was trying to say with them. I used to run, and even if I wasn’t fast or anything, there was a feeling to it. Basketball too—watching it, playing a little, talking about it. And even at work, making a really good drink, getting it just right, that used to give me some pride.

Now I just kind of stand there. I look at the same stuff and it’s like… nothing. Like I’m watching someone else’s life from across the room. I don’t care about any of it the way I used to, and that’s what scared me enough to come in.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has experienced a loss of interest or pleasure in activities they once enjoyed, a key symptom of depression.
doctor.question: Can you tell me if you’ve lost interest in those activities completely, or if you still want to do them but just can’t seem to feel anything from them?

target_item.name: Loss_of_Interest

patient.answer:
I think it’s more like… I don’t even really want to do them anymore, not in the way I used to. Or maybe I go through the motion of wanting to, because I remember that I used to be that person. Like with murals, I’ll see one and I know, in my head, that normally I’d stop and look at the details, the colors, the way the lines are done, all of that. I used to get this little spark from it. Now I just look at it and it’s flat. Like it has nothing to do with me.

Same with running or basketball. It’s not even that I’m sitting there wishing I could enjoy it and then failing. It’s more like the wanting part got shut off too. And at work, making a good drink… I know when I’ve done it right, I know what it’s supposed to feel like to take pride in that, but I just kind of stand there and do it. It doesn’t land anywhere.

So I guess the honest answer is both, but mostly I’ve lost interest. I don’t care about any of it the way I used to, and that’s what scared me.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has experienced a depressed mood most of the day, nearly every day, which is a key criterion for major depressive disorder.
doctor.question: Have you noticed that your mood has been down or depressed most of the time, even outside of not feeling interested in those activities?

target_item.reason: The question is directly asking about persistently depressed mood, but the provided symptom profile does not include a separate item for depressed mood.

patient.answer:
I’m not totally sure how to separate those things, honestly. Like… I don’t walk around thinking, “I’m sad,” exactly. It’s not always that clear. A lot of the time it’s more like everything is heavy or muted, like the color got turned down on the whole day.

But if you mean, do I feel low even when I’m not specifically thinking about murals or running or work or whatever… yeah, I think so. I mean, I don’t know if I’d call it depressed every minute, because sometimes I’m just kind of blank, or I’m distracted by whatever I’m doing. But underneath it, there’s this dragged-down feeling that seems to be there most of the time.

It’s hard to explain because I keep second-guessing myself. Like maybe I’m just tired, or maybe I’m just in a bad stretch. But it doesn’t really lift the way a normal bad mood would. It’s just there, kind of sitting on everything.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient experiences additional core symptoms of depression such as changes in appetite, sleep disturbances, or feelings of worthlessness, which would support a diagnosis of major depressive disorder.
doctor.question: Have you noticed any changes in your sleep or appetite lately, or do you find yourself feeling worse about yourself than usual?

target_item.name: Sleep_Disturbance
target_item.manifestation: I lie down tired but my head keeps going over every mistake I made at work, and when I finally sleep I wake up around four or five and can't get back down.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about changes in sleep, appetite, and self-worth; sleep disturbance is one directly asked-about symptom and should be answered with this profile item.

patient.answer:
Yeah… sleep, definitely. I mean, appetite I’m not really sure how to answer right now, but sleep has been bad.

I’ll be exhausted by the time I lie down, like my body feels completely done, especially after work. But as soon as I’m in bed, my head just starts going. It’s like it picks up every little thing I did wrong that day and plays it back at me.
